title: Seven ears of grain
hookLine: a gift in Allah's way is like a grain that grows seven ears, a hundred grains each (2:261)
last: HE CAN REVIVE WHAT IS DEAD.

cards: Pull one stalk of wheat from a field and look at the top. The ear is packed with grains in neat rows. Any farmer knows the trade: one grain in the ground, and months later you hold dozens.
Arithmetic and hope in the same handful. Right after three stories about God bringing the dead to life, al-Baqarah turns to the field and does some arithmetic of its own.

teach.h: ONE GRAIN, SEVEN EARS, A HUNDRED EACH
teach.b: Verse two hundred sixty-one, in Pickthall's words: “The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains.”
Do the math: seven hundred. And the verse adds: God multiplies for whom He wills.
Seven hundred isn't the ceiling. The placement matters. The surah has just shown a dead town, a donkey's bones, four birds, all brought to life.
Now a seed, buried and dead-looking, brings up a field.
Giving is pictured the same way: let go into the ground, lost-looking, and coming back multiplied. Two hadith fill in the picture.
A hadith qudsi in Bukhari and Muslim says a good deed is written as ten, up to seven hundred times, and many times more.

Another, in Bukhari, says that whoever gives even the value of a single date from honest earnings, God accepts it with His right hand and raises it the way one of you raises a young horse, until it becomes like a mountain.
One date. The grain in the verse is tiny too. Nothing here asks for a large gift.
It asks for a real one, given for God's sake, from what's honestly yours, and then let go. In the verse, the arithmetic is God's.

how: Muslims give sadaqah, voluntary charity, in amounts large and small, often citing 2:261 and the hadith that even a date given from honest earnings grows like a mountain.

games.q: you only have a little to give today: the value of one date. what does the hadith in Bukhari say?
o: give it; God raises it until it's like a mountain.
games.why: give it: from honest earnings, God accepts it with His right hand and raises it like a foal until it's like a mountain.

practice: Choose one small gift, a coin, a meal, ten minutes of help, and where it could go: a charity, a neighbor, someone on the street, a colleague who's struggling.
Picture handing it over and letting it go, like a grain into the soil, without needing to see what grows.

wordCard.voice: Sunbulah, an ear of grain: al-Baqarah's picture of giving, one grain that grows seven ears, a hundred grains each.

orig.note: Arabic: ears of grain (singular sunbulah); the seven ears of 2:261.

carryVoice: Your line: one grain, seven hundred. The gift can be as small as a date. I'll keep a seat for you.
